findings.location: query_similar_tasks -> candidates CTE (the only query_* without a category/outcome predicate)
findings.finding: Task rows are stored with outcome='completed'|'blocked' and the model-default category='task' (models.py:754-756), while every other write site stores a distinct outcome/category. query_similar_tasks filters on neither, so a failure/preference/bug/prompt-change row is returned as a 'similar past task'. Because query_memory_context (684-696) also runs the 7 category-specific queries, the same non-task row can appear twice in one injected block — once under 'Similar past tasks' (format_memory_context, 837-851) and once under its own section (format_full_memory_context, 757-834).
findings.evidence: store.py:609-621 (WHERE = embedding NOT NULL + vector_norm>0 + archived=false + repo filter only); write sites verified for all 8 categories; models.py:754-756 (category default 'task'); consumed by memory_hook_node on every agent run (base_graph.py:1652-1670), the pipeline prefetch (pipeline/graph.py:245-258 -> state.py:24 -> pm.py:130-131,156 / architect.py:146,160 / decomposer.py:153,159), and GET /api/memory/search (api/memory.py:157-159). No test pins the expected behavior: test_b4_memory_categories.py:248-294 only exercises the archived filter; test at 143-188 seeds all categories with identical text and asserts non-emptiness only.
findings.production_impact: The top-3 'similar past tasks' slots injected into every agent's prompt can be entirely non-task rows, mislabeled by their outcome string; duplicated rows waste the 3000-token injection budget (config.py:673-680) and dilute retrieval precision. Silent — nothing logs the mixing.
findings.confidence: High (SQL verified; absence of filter is unambiguous)
findings.recommendation: Add AND category = 'task' (or outcome IN ('completed','blocked')) to the candidates CTE; add a real-DB test seeding all 8 categories and asserting the tasks section contains only task rows.

findings.location: _versioned_lesson_consolidation_loop — consolidation branch vs the 'Also repair' block
findings.finding: Loop body is: sleep -> try { if not memory_consolidation_enabled: continue; consolidate() } -> also reembed_zero_vector_rows(). When an operator sets MEMORY_CONSOLIDATION_ENABLED=false (a documented, supported switch — config.py:1715-1717, loop docstring 250-253), the continue restarts the loop and skips the zero-vector repair block entirely. reembed_zero_vector_rows has no other scheduled caller in production (only call site main.py:277-280; store.py:425 def; tests only).
findings.evidence: main.py:259-260 vs 273-284; comment at 273-274 documents the repair as an independent concern, but control flow couples it to the consolidation switch. reembed_zero_vector_rows no-ops without a key (store.py:432-433) and repairs <=50 rows/cycle (limit default at 426).
findings.production_impact: After a Voyage outage (or any backlog of dead rows), an operator who disables consolidation — precisely the cost-conscious configuration — silently loses the only automatic recovery path for rows deliberately written "stored... but dead" (test_b4_memory_store.py:260-285). Dead rows stay unsearchable until a key appears and repair runs, or 180-day retention archives them.
findings.recommendation: Move the repair block above the continue (own try/except, own cadence), or restructure as two independent guarded sections; give repair its own switch if the coupling is unwanted by design.

findings.finding: For one identical description, the 7 sub-queries each perform their own Voyage embedding round-trip (via _embed, which also runs the sync client in a thread) and are awaited strictly serially, followed by up to 7 record_memory_access updates. The sync bridge additionally creates a throwaway DB engine + a fresh event loop per agent run. With VOYAGE_API_KEY set (the production-config case) this is 7 duplicate HTTP calls for one text per agent run start; with no key it short-circuits cheaply (zero-vector, 597-598).
findings.evidence: Cited lines; callers: every agent run (memory_hook_node, base_graph.py:1629-1678) — cost multiplies by concurrent runs (max_concurrent_agent_runs=20, config.py:804-805); the pipeline prefetch (graph.py:257) calls only query_similar_tasks (single embed) — the 7x cost is the agent-run path.
findings.production_impact: ~1-3 s of serialized provider latency added before every agent's inference when the key is configured (plus 7 DB round-trips); 20 concurrent runs emit 140 embedding requests for 20 unique texts. Invisible in metrics except the aggregate memory_retrieval phase timing.
findings.confidence: High (code path); Medium on exact latency magnitude (provider-dependent)
findings.recommendation: Embed once in query_memory_context and pass the vector (or a lazy embedder) into the sub-queries; consider asyncio.gather for the independent reads; optionally reuse a single engine for the sync bridge.

findings.file: backend/app/memory/store.py (+ inaccurate claim in backend/app/agents/base_graph.py comment)
findings.location: write path embed_task_outcome (and siblings) vs _embed / _find_near_duplicate / reembed_zero_vector_rows
findings.finding: With voyage_api_key unset (the config default, config.py:41-43) and memory_enabled=true (default), every agent run still inserts task-outcome/failure/architecture rows with a zero embedding: dedup is skipped, the quality gate passes real content, and the insert is unconditional. Those rows are invisible to every query (vector_norm(embedding) > 0, 616-617) and can never self-heal — repair explicitly no-ops without a key. The base_graph.py:3199-3204 comment justifies skipping the versioned-lesson publish with 'same meaning-without-a-key logic app.memory.store already uses' — but store.py's zero-vector logic is query-side only; it does not skip these writes, so the claimed precedent is not what the code does.
findings.evidence: Cited lines; tests/test_b4_memory_store.py:260-285 proves 'stored... but dead' is the intended behavior for a provider outage (write now, repair later) — the no-key case shares that path but has no recovery until a key is configured, then repairs <=50 rows per 24 h cycle (main.py:280, memory_consolidation_interval_hours=24).
findings.production_impact: In any deployment without a Voyage key, memory_embeddings grows with permanently unusable rows (analytics count them; composite ranking never sees them); if a key is added later, a large backlog clears at <=50 rows/day. The misleading comment raises the risk that reviewers believe no such rows exist.
findings.confidence: High (behavior) / Medium (whether preserve-raw-text-for-later-embedding was a deliberate decision for the no-key case)
findings.recommendation: Gate the write on a real key (skip insert when voyage_api_key absent — mirroring the versioned-publish gate at base_graph.py:3207), or keep write-and-repair but document it explicitly in the _embed docstring and raise/uncouple the repair rate; fix the base_graph.py:3199-3204 wording.

findings.line: 25-38 (set has 7 values — no prompt_change); 60-63 (unknown values silently ignored, no 4xx)
findings.finding: prompt_change has been a real, written category since #405 (store.py:1991-1992; query at 2168; writer caller prompt_registry.py:354,370) but is absent from the endpoint's filter set and its own description string (memory.py:46). A request for it (or any typo like ?category=failures) falls through the 'in' check and returns the unfiltered aggregate/recent list instead of an error or a filtered result.
findings.evidence: Cited lines; the set's own comment (30-34) shows it was maintained by hand once (procedure/preference/bug added) and missed the newer category.
findings.production_impact: A dashboard filtering by category can silently display an all-categories feed; consumers cannot distinguish 'no data' from 'filter ignored'. Read-only surface — no data corruption.
findings.recommendation: Single shared category constant (e.g. export the 8 values from store/models) used by both the API and writers; return 422 for unknown values.

findings.line: 621 (_lesson_lock(topic)); 622 + 115-138 (_find_most_similar_published — global, no topic filter); 642-650 (merged draft reuses lesson_id, version+1); 141-172 (_insert, no uniqueness); 218-244 (promote picks version DESC LIMIT 1, no tiebreaker)
findings.finding: Two concurrent publish() calls on different topics take different advisory locks but each performs a fleet-wide similarity check. If both texts are >= memory_merge_similarity_threshold (0.85) against the same published lesson, both insert a merged draft with the same lesson_id and same version number. promote() then selects one draft by version DESC LIMIT 1 with no secondary ordering (tie -> arbitrary); the other stays draft and could be promoted later, publishing a second same-lineage row without flipping the first (promote only flips supersedes_id).
findings.evidence: Cited lines. Design docstrings claim serialization by topic (67-112) and the consolidation sweep has its own __consolidation_sweep__ lock (684) — but publish() never takes it.
findings.production_impact: Duplicate draft/published versions within one lineage after concurrent similar lesson extraction (publish is called per agent run when a key is set, base_graph.py:3212). Data is not lost; history/version numbering becomes ambiguous and rollback can flip the 'wrong' sibling. Narrow window; requires two >=0.85-similar publishes against one lesson on different topics.
findings.confidence: Medium (mechanism verified in code; real-world frequency unproven)
findings.recommendation: Constrain the match to the same topic inside the lock, take a global publish/merge lock (reuse __consolidation_sweep__), or add a DB uniqueness constraint on (lesson_id, version) plus a tiebreaker in _most_recent_draft_for_lineage.
